entry.title: Jack Whitehall: ‘Stirring Up’ Rivalries & Roasting F1 Drivers | F1 Beyond The Grid Podcast

media:group.media:title: Jack Whitehall: ‘Stirring Up’ Rivalries & Roasting F1 Drivers | F1 Beyond The Grid Podcast
media:group.media:description:
‘Cheer up Max it could have be worse, at least we didn’t sit you next to George Russell’. Jack Whitehall’s joke at F1 75 Live still feels topical nearly two years later. Jack was hired to poke fun at the sport’s biggest names, but at heart he’s a racing fan who admires the drivers’ skill as much as he admires Charles Leclerc’s eyes.
A regular in the paddock and an official ‘Friend of F1’, Jack tells Tom Clarkson what he loves about the sport, what racing has in common with stand-up comedy, and why ‘impish’ Kimi Antonelli is unlike any other sportsperson he’s met.
Jack also talks fearing for his life on a hot lap with Valtteri Bottas, being teased by Lewis Hamilton for not being able to drive, checking jokes with George Russell, Toto Wolff’s roast request and the former schoolmate who beat him to the role of James Bond.

entry.title: Max & George Reignite Rivalry & What Next For Ferrari? | Las Vegas GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast

media:group.media:title: Max & George Reignite Rivalry & What Next For Ferrari? | Las Vegas GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast
media:group.media:description:
AWS - Global AI Partner of Formula 1 - sponsors this episode of F1 Nation.
Jolyon Palmer, Alex Jacques and Tom Clarkson are catching their breath in the paddock after a crazy Las Vegas Grand Prix.
With 35 passes for the lead, how did Max Verstappen come out on top? What did his race craft and capacity to think about strategy tell us? And where does this victory rank among Max’s other 74?
Tom, Jolyon and Alex analyse an ‘exquisite’ performance from the four-time World Champion and share their thoughts on the war of words that has broken out between Verstappen and George Russell in Vegas, following their incident in the final practice session.
Also up for debate is what action Ferrari take after Charles Leclerc’s collision with teammate Lewis Hamilton. Should the drivers be punished by the team? If so, how? You’ll hear reaction from Charles, Lewis and Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur.
Plus, the guys discuss a double podium for McLaren, why Mercedes missed out on the win, a ‘rookie error’ from Arvid Lindblad and big results for Alpine and Carlos Sainz.
